status_summary: A senators' letter of 2025-11-21 says the current White House Counsel adopted a new contacts policy with the Justice Department; the policy itself is not public, and its reported terms could not be confirmed from an opened primary or news source. On 2025-10-22 the nominee to lead the Criminal Division said a new DOJ contacts policy was forthcoming, and on 2025-10-24 he wrote that the existing policy had not been rescinded and remained in the Justice Manual (Bloomberg Government, 2025-10-29). Justice Manual section 1-8.600, read on justice.gov on 2026-10-18, still reproduces the Attorney General's memorandum of 2021-07-21 and shows no revision after April 2022, and senators said on 2026-06-25 that DOJ had not answered their records request on the policy. No document authorizing channels beyond the Counsel's office and the Attorney General or Deputy Attorney General was found, so the reexamination is reported but has no documented operative result.

timeline.event: Baseline: Counsel to the President Dana Remus issues a policy under which only the President, Vice President, Counsel or a Deputy Counsel may initiate White House contacts with DOJ about particular contemplated or pending criminal or civil investigations and cases, outside national security matters.

Baseline: Attorney General Garland issues a memorandum on Department of Justice communications with the White House. The Department will not advise the White House on pending or contemplated investigations or cases unless important to the President's duties and appropriate from a law enforcement perspective; initial contacts on such matters involve the Attorney General or Deputy Attorney General (and, in civil matters, the Associate Attorney General) with the White House Counsel or a Deputy Counsel, the President or the Vice President; national security communications with NSC staff are largely exempt.

USA Today reports that a Feb. 9 memo lowered guardrails on contact between DOJ and White House officials; the article does not say who issued it, and a former DOJ lawyer quoted in it is critical of the change.

At his Senate Judiciary confirmation hearing, Tysen Duva, nominee to lead DOJ's Criminal Division, says a new policy on DOJ and White House contacts in criminal cases is forthcoming and under review by the Attorney General and Deputy Attorney General, and that a start-of-administration blanket memo had rescinded prior policies including the contacts policy.

Duva writes to Senate Judiciary leaders that he misspoke: the White House contacts policy has not been rescinded and is publicly available in the Justice Manual; his statement that an updated policy is coming is not retracted (reported 2025-10-29).

Sens. Whitehouse, Blumenthal and Schiff file a FOIA request with DOJ for records of Attorney General Bondi's meetings with the White House Counsel on the contacts policy; their letter says the Justice Manual holds the previous administration's policy and that a new policy adopted by the current Counsel raises compatibility questions.

A release from Sens. Whitehouse and Blumenthal says the Justice Department has failed to respond to their FOIA requests, including one on DOJ's White House contacts policy, as Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's confirmation hearing is set for 2026-07-15.

title: Reexamine the White House Counsel and Attorney General contact policy with DOJ
uncertainties: The 2025 White House Counsel policy is not public. Its reported terms (that the President, Vice President, Counsel and a Deputy Counsel may each start contacts about any specific criminal or civil case or investigation) are attributed to Washington Post reporting of February 2025 that was not opened, so they are unverified; a USA Today piece does not identify the issuer of the Feb. 9 memo, so the memo's date, author and terms are unconfirmed; the senators' letter of 2025-11-21 confirms only that the current Counsel adopted a new policy and does not describe its contents, and it asks for records on 'the adoption of the previous administration's policy', which the record does not resolve. The Bloomberg Government articles are partly paywalled; the correction article states that the Justice Manual policy was not rescinded, but its text was read only in part. The Justice Manual page (section 1-8.600) was read on justice.gov on 2026-10-08 and still carries the 2021 memorandum, with the section marked updated April 2022 (Bloomberg Government's reference to a 2022 policy appears to reflect that update); a revision published elsewhere, or a policy not posted in the Manual, would not show there. No published DOJ policy replacing the 2021 one was found; the absence also rests on the senators' June 2026 release and web searches on Blanche, Bondi and Duva. Whether written questions put to Blanche in July 2026 addressed the policy, and any answers, could not be verified from a primary or news source. The senators' release is a party press statement. Searches run: DOJ new policy contacts with White House 2026 and Blanche; Blanche hearing and contacts policy; Warrington memo; Justice Manual 1-8.000; Warrington memo contacts policy. Justice Manual section 1-8.600 (Communication with the White House) on justice.gov was re-read on 2026-10-08 and again on 2026-10-18: it still reproduces the Attorney General's 2021-07-21 memorandum in full, is marked updated April 2022 and cites no 2025 or 2026 revision. The Attorney General memoranda of 2025-02-05 listed on justice.gov include none on White House contacts, as far as their titles show. Two searches on 2026-10-22 for the Washington Post report on the Counsel policy found no openable copy; a regional newspaper e-edition page that may reprint related reporting could not be opened.
